_about: This file was assembled by hand from pokemondb and bulbapedia before any
Champions-native source was available. hk then supplied a table compiled
from the game's v1.2.0 data and checked it themselves, which
scripts/import_patch_table.py reads into mc_table.json. That has all 32
species with types, base stats, abilities *and* learnsets, and it is the
What is kept here is the comparison, because it says how far the dex can
be trusted, and one correction that matters more than the rest.
the_correction: I mistranslated two Korean names and built an argument on it.
갑주무사 is Golisopod, not Samurott -- Samurott is 대검귀. So Golisopod's
Emergency Exit is its ordinary mainline ability and nothing was changed.
The claim that 'Champions rewrote a base species' ability, so trust no
ability in the dex' was my error, not a finding.
케오퍼스 is Grapploct, not Clodsire -- Clodsire is 토오. That one came
from a web search that answered confidently and wrongly.
Both were avoidable: data/champions/names.json had them.

how_far_the_dex_can_be_trusted.checked: all 32 species of the M-C update, against the game's own table
how_far_the_dex_can_be_trusted.abilities: 27 of 32. The five wrong are exactly the Champions-original Megas -- Mega Absol Z, Mega Garchomp Z, Mega Lucario Z, Mega Golisopod and Mega Baxcalibur -- where Showdown carries the base species' abilities instead.
how_far_the_dex_can_be_trusted.so: Showdown's numbers are sound and so are its abilities for species that exist in the mainline games. What it cannot know is a forme Champions invented. That is a much narrower rule than the one I wrote yesterday, and it is what the evidence supports.

still_open: The roster itself: regulation M-C, not M-B. fetch_regulation.py takes a name.
Existing species gained and lost moves as well -- the table lists those changes and they are not in mc_table.json yet.
Two move powers changed: 베어가르기 70 -> 80, 스타어설트 150 -> 170.
One move removed from the format: 막치기.
